question: For the season's top run scorer (runs off the bat), in which city or cities did they score the most runs? Return all tied cities with the runs.
gold_sql: WITH c AS (SELECT v.city, SUM(d.runs_of_bat) AS r, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY SUM(d.runs_of_bat) DESC) AS rk FROM deliveries d JOIN matches m ON m.match_id = d.match_id JOIN venues v ON v.venue_id = m.venue_id WHERE d.striker_id = (SELECT striker_id FROM deliveries GROUP BY striker_id ORDER BY SUM(runs_of_bat) DESC LIMIT 1) GROUP BY v.city) SELECT city, r FROM c WHERE rk = 1
model_sql:
WITH top_scorer AS (
  SELECT striker_id
  FROM deliveries
  GROUP BY striker_id
  ORDER BY SUM(runs_of_bat) DESC
  LIMIT 1
),
city_runs AS (
  SELECT 
    v.city,
    SUM(d.runs_of_bat) as runs
  FROM deliveries d
  JOIN matches m ON d.match_id = m.match_id
  JOIN venues v ON m.venue_id = v.venue_id
  WHERE d.striker_id = (SELECT striker_id FROM top_scorer)
  GROUP BY v.city
)
SELECT city, runs
FROM city_runs
WHERE runs = (SELECT MAX(runs) FROM city_runs)
ORDER BY city

question: Compare the average team innings total (runs off the bat plus extras, regular innings) when a team bats at one of its own home venues versus anywhere else. Ignore matches marked abandoned in match_results. Return labels 'home' and 'away' with the averages.
gold_sql: WITH t AS (SELECT d.match_id, d.batting_team, SUM(d.runs_of_bat + d.extras) AS r FROM deliveries d WHERE d.innings <= 2 AND d.match_id NOT IN (SELECT match_id FROM match_results WHERE match_result = 'abandoned') GROUP BY d.match_id, d.batting_team) SELECT CASE WHEN v.home_team = t.batting_team THEN 'home' ELSE 'away' END AS side, AVG(t.r) FROM t JOIN matches m ON m.match_id = t.match_id JOIN venues v ON v.venue_id = m.venue_id GROUP BY side
model_sql:
WITH team_innings AS (
  SELECT
    d.match_id,
    d.batting_team,
    d.innings,
    m.venue_id,
    v.home_team,
    SUM(d.runs_of_bat + d.extras) AS innings_total
  FROM deliveries d
  JOIN matches m ON d.match_id = m.match_id
  JOIN venues v ON m.venue_id = v.venue_id
  WHERE d.innings IN (1, 2)
  GROUP BY d.match_id, d.batting_team, d.innings
),
filtered_innings AS (
  SELECT
    ti.match_id,
    ti.batting_team,
    ti.innings_total,
    CASE WHEN ti.batting_team = ti.home_team THEN 'home' ELSE 'away' END AS venue_type
  FROM team_innings ti
  WHERE NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM match_results mr
    WHERE mr.match_id = ti.match_id AND mr.match_result = 'abandoned'
  )
)
SELECT
  venue_type,
  AVG(innings_total) AS average_innings_total
FROM filtered_innings
GROUP BY venue_type
ORDER BY venue_type

question: How many centuries (100+ runs off the bat in a match) were scored in a losing cause? Only matches with a completed result in match_results can be judged.
gold_sql: WITH c AS (SELECT d.match_id, d.batting_team FROM deliveries d WHERE d.innings <= 2 GROUP BY d.match_id, d.striker_id HAVING SUM(d.runs_of_bat) >= 100) SELECT COUNT(*) FROM c JOIN match_results r ON r.match_id = c.match_id WHERE r.match_result = 'completed' AND r.match_winner != c.batting_team
model_sql:
WITH match_info AS (
  SELECT 
    match_id,
    match_winner,
    CASE 
      WHEN home_team = match_winner THEN away_team
      WHEN away_team = match_winner THEN home_team
    END AS losing_team
  FROM match_results
  WHERE match_result = 'completed'
),
batter_runs AS (
  SELECT 
    d.match_id,
    d.batting_team,
    d.striker_id,
    SUM(d.runs_of_bat) AS runs_off_bat
  FROM deliveries d
  WHERE d.innings IN (1, 2)
  GROUP BY d.match_id, d.batting_team, d.striker_id
)
SELECT COUNT(*) AS centuries_in_losing_cause
FROM batter_runs br
JOIN match_info mi ON br.match_id = mi.match_id
WHERE br.batting_team = mi.losing_team
  AND br.runs_off_bat >= 100

question: Among bowlers with at least 120 legal deliveries (regular innings), who has the best economy rate (runs conceded per 6 legal balls; byes and leg-byes are not charged)? Give the name and economy.
gold_sql: SELECT p.player_name, 6.0 * SUM(d.runs_of_bat + CASE WHEN d.wide = 1 OR d.noballs = 1 THEN d.extras ELSE 0 END) / SUM(CASE WHEN d.wide = 0 AND d.noballs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS econ FROM deliveries d JOIN players p ON p.player_id = d.bowler_id WHERE d.innings <= 2 GROUP BY p.player_id HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN d.wide = 0 AND d.noballs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) >= 120 ORDER BY econ ASC LIMIT 1
model_sql:
WITH bowler_stats AS (
  SELECT
    d.bowler_id,
    p.player_name,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE d.wide = 0 AND d.noballs = 0) AS legal_deliveries,
    SUM(d.runs_of_bat + d.extras - d.byes - d.legbyes) FILTER (WHERE d.wide = 0 AND d.noballs = 0) AS runs_conceded
  FROM deliveries d
  JOIN players p ON d.bowler_id = p.player_id
  WHERE d.innings IN (1, 2)
  GROUP BY d.bowler_id, p.player_name
  HAVING COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE d.wide = 0 AND d.noballs = 0) >= 120
)
SELECT
  player_name,
  (runs_conceded * 6.0) / legal_deliveries AS economy
FROM bowler_stats
ORDER BY economy ASC
LIMIT 1

question: Which bowling team had the best (lowest) economy in the death overs (overs 15-19, regular innings)? Economy = runs conceded per 6 legal balls (byes and leg-byes not charged). Give the full team name and economy.
gold_sql: SELECT t.team_name, 6.0 * SUM(d.runs_of_bat + CASE WHEN d.wide = 1 OR d.noballs = 1 THEN d.extras ELSE 0 END) / SUM(CASE WHEN d.wide = 0 AND d.noballs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS econ FROM deliveries d JOIN teams t ON t.team_code = d.bowling_team WHERE d.innings <= 2 AND d.over_no >= 15 GROUP BY t.team_code ORDER BY econ ASC LIMIT 1
model_sql:
WITH death_overs AS (
  SELECT 
    bowling_team,
    SUM(runs_of_bat + CASE WHEN wide = 0 AND noballs = 0 THEN extras ELSE 0 END) as runs_conceded,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE wide = 0 AND noballs = 0) as legal_balls
  FROM deliveries
  WHERE over_no >= 15 
    AND over_no <= 19 
    AND innings IN (1, 2)
    AND wide = 0 
    AND noballs = 0
  GROUP BY bowling_team
)
SELECT 
  t.team_name,
  CAST(d.runs_conceded AS REAL) / (d.legal_balls / 6.0) as economy
FROM death_overs d
JOIN teams t ON d.bowling_team = t.team_code
ORDER BY economy ASC
LIMIT 1

question: In how many matches does match_results.highscore differ from the runs off the bat that the listed top scorer actually made in that match according to deliveries (regular innings only)?
gold_sql: WITH s AS (SELECT match_id, striker_id, SUM(runs_of_bat) AS r FROM deliveries WHERE innings <= 2 GROUP BY match_id, striker_id) SELECT COUNT(*) FROM match_results mr JOIN s ON s.match_id = mr.match_id AND s.striker_id = mr.top_scorer_id WHERE mr.highscore != s.r
model_sql:
WITH player_runs AS (
  SELECT 
    d.match_id,
    d.striker_id,
    SUM(d.runs_of_bat) as actual_runs_off_bat
  FROM deliveries d
  WHERE d.innings IN (1, 2)
  GROUP BY d.match_id, d.striker_id
)
SELECT COUNT(*) as count
FROM match_results mr
WHERE mr.top_scorer_id IS NOT NULL
  AND mr.highscore IS NOT NULL
  AND EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM player_runs pr
    WHERE pr.match_id = mr.match_id
      AND pr.striker_id = mr.top_scorer_id

  )

question: Which team(s) used the most different players this season (anyone who batted, bowled or fielded for it)? Return all tied teams (full names) with the number of players.
gold_sql: WITH used AS (SELECT batting_team AS team, striker_id AS pid FROM deliveries UNION SELECT bowling_team, bowler_id FROM deliveries UNION SELECT d.bowling_team, f.player_id FROM delivery_fielders f JOIN deliveries d ON d.delivery_id = f.delivery_id), c AS (SELECT team, COUNT(*) AS n, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC) AS rk FROM used GROUP BY team) SELECT t.team_name, c.n FROM c JOIN teams t ON t.team_code = c.team WHERE c.rk = 1
model_sql:
WITH team_players AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT batting_team AS team_code, striker_id AS player_id
  FROM deliveries
  UNION
  SELECT DISTINCT bowling_team AS team_code, bowler_id AS player_id
  FROM deliveries
  UNION
  SELECT DISTINCT batting_team AS team_code, player_dismissed_id AS player_id
  FROM deliveries
  WHERE player_dismissed_id IS NOT NULL
  UNION
  SELECT DISTINCT bowling_team AS team_code, player_id
  FROM delivery_fielders
  JOIN deliveries ON delivery_fielders.delivery_id = deliveries.delivery_id
)
SELECT t.team_name, COUNT(DISTINCT tp.player_id) AS player_count
FROM team_players tp
JOIN teams t ON tp.team_code = t.team_code
GROUP BY tp.team_code, t.team_name
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT tp.player_id) = (
  SELECT MAX(player_count)
  FROM (
    SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT player_id) AS player_count
    FROM team_players
    GROUP BY team_code
  )
)
ORDER BY t.team_name

question: Which team had the biggest increase in its innings total (runs off the bat plus extras, regular innings) from one match to its next match in date order? Ignore matches marked abandoned in match_results. Give the full team name and the increase.
gold_sql: WITH t AS (SELECT d.match_id, d.batting_team, SUM(d.runs_of_bat + d.extras) AS r FROM deliveries d WHERE d.innings <= 2 AND d.match_id NOT IN (SELECT match_id FROM match_results WHERE match_result = 'abandoned') GROUP BY d.match_id, d.batting_team), g AS (SELECT t.batting_team, t.r - LAG(t.r) OVER (PARTITION BY t.batting_team ORDER BY m.date, m.match_id) AS diff FROM t JOIN matches m ON m.match_id = t.match_id) SELECT tm.team_name, g.diff FROM g JOIN teams tm ON tm.team_code = g.batting_team ORDER BY g.diff DESC LIMIT 1
model_sql:
WITH match_innings_totals AS (
  SELECT 
    m.match_id,
    m.date,
    d.batting_team,
    t.team_name,
    SUM(d.runs_of_bat + d.extras) AS innings_total,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY d.batting_team ORDER BY m.date) AS match_seq
  FROM deliveries d
  JOIN matches m ON d.match_id = m.match_id
  JOIN teams t ON d.batting_team = t.team_code
  LEFT JOIN match_results mr ON m.match_id = mr.match_id
  WHERE d.innings IN (1, 2)
    AND (mr.match_result IS NULL OR mr.match_result != 'abandoned')
  GROUP BY m.match_id, d.batting_team, m.date, t.team_name
),
consecutive_matches AS (
  SELECT 
    curr.batting_team,
    curr.team_name,
    curr.innings_total AS current_total,
    LAG(curr.innings_total) OVER (PARTITION BY curr.batting_team ORDER BY curr.match_seq) AS prev_total,
    curr.innings_total - LAG(curr.innings_total) OVER (PARTITION BY curr.batting_team ORDER BY curr.match_seq) AS increase
  FROM match_innings_totals curr
)
SELECT 
  team_name,
  increase
FROM consecutive_matches
WHERE increase IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY increase DESC
LIMIT 1

question: How many ducks were there this season? A duck is a player dismissed in a match (regular innings, excluding 'retired hurt') who scored zero runs off the bat in that match, including players dismissed without facing a ball.
gold_sql: WITH dis AS (SELECT DISTINCT match_id, player_dismissed_id AS pid FROM deliveries WHERE player_dismissed_id IS NOT NULL AND wicket_type != 'retired hurt' AND innings <= 2), runs AS (SELECT match_id, striker_id AS pid, SUM(runs_of_bat) AS r FROM deliveries WHERE innings <= 2 GROUP BY match_id, striker_id) SELECT COUNT(*) FROM dis LEFT JOIN runs ON runs.match_id = dis.match_id AND runs.pid = dis.pid WHERE COALESCE(runs.r, 0) = 0
model_sql:
WITH player_match_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    d.match_id,
    d.batting_team,
    d.striker_id,
    SUM(d.runs_of_bat) as total_runs_of_bat,
    MAX(CASE WHEN d.player_dismissed_id IS NOT NULL AND d.wicket_type != 'retired hurt' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as was_dismissed
  FROM deliveries d
  WHERE d.innings IN (1, 2)
  GROUP BY d.match_id, d.batting_team, d.striker_id
)
SELECT COUNT(*) as duck_count
FROM player_match_stats
WHERE was_dismissed = 1 AND total_runs_of_bat = 0

question: What is the highest score by a batter who was NOT dismissed in that match (a not-out innings, regular innings only)? Give the name and runs.
gold_sql: WITH s AS (SELECT match_id, striker_id, SUM(runs_of_bat) AS r FROM deliveries WHERE innings <= 2 GROUP BY match_id, striker_id) SELECT p.player_name, s.r FROM s JOIN players p ON p.player_id = s.striker_id WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM deliveries d WHERE d.match_id = s.match_id AND d.player_dismissed_id = s.striker_id AND d.innings <= 2) ORDER BY s.r DESC LIMIT 1
model_sql:
SELECT 
    p.player_name,
    MAX(d.runs_of_bat + d.extras) as runs
FROM deliveries d
JOIN players p ON d.striker_id = p.player_id
JOIN matches m ON d.match_id = m.match_id
WHERE d.innings IN (1, 2)
    AND d.player_dismissed_id IS NULL
GROUP BY d.match_id, d.innings, d.striker_id, p.player_name
ORDER BY runs DESC
LIMIT 1

question: Which bowler bowled the most maiden overs? A maiden is an over (same match, innings, over number and bowler; regular innings) with exactly 6 legal deliveries and zero runs conceded (byes and leg-byes are not charged). Give the name and count.
gold_sql: WITH o AS (SELECT d.bowler_id, SUM(d.runs_of_bat + CASE WHEN d.wide = 1 OR d.noballs = 1 THEN d.extras ELSE 0 END) AS conceded, SUM(CASE WHEN d.wide = 0 AND d.noballs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS legal FROM deliveries d WHERE d.innings <= 2 GROUP BY d.match_id, d.innings, d.over_no, d.bowler_id) SELECT p.player_name, COUNT(*) AS maidens FROM o JOIN players p ON p.player_id = o.bowler_id WHERE o.conceded = 0 AND o.legal = 6 GROUP BY p.player_id ORDER BY maidens DESC LIMIT 1
model_sql:
WITH maiden_overs AS (
  SELECT 
    bowler_id,
    match_id,
    innings,
    over_no,
    COUNT(*) as legal_balls,
    SUM(runs_of_bat + CASE WHEN wide = 0 AND noballs = 0 THEN 0 ELSE extras END) as runs_conceded
  FROM deliveries
  WHERE innings IN (1, 2)
    AND wide = 0
    AND noballs = 0
  GROUP BY bowler_id, match_id, innings, over_no
  HAVING COUNT(*) = 6 AND SUM(runs_of_bat + CASE WHEN wide = 0 AND noballs = 0 THEN 0 ELSE extras END) = 0
)
SELECT 
  p.player_name,
  COUNT(*) as maiden_overs
FROM maiden_overs m
JOIN players p ON m.bowler_id = p.player_id
GROUP BY m.bowler_id, p.player_name
ORDER BY maiden_overs DESC
LIMIT 1

question: How many times did a player score at least 30 runs off the bat AND take at least 2 bowler-credited wickets in the same match (regular innings)?
gold_sql: WITH bat AS (SELECT match_id, striker_id AS pid, SUM(runs_of_bat) AS r FROM deliveries WHERE innings <= 2 GROUP BY match_id, striker_id), bowl AS (SELECT d.match_id, d.bowler_id AS pid, COUNT(*) AS w FROM deliveries d WHERE d.innings <= 2 AND d.player_dismissed_id IS NOT NULL AND d.wicket_type NOT IN ('run out','retired hurt','obstructing the field') GROUP BY d.match_id, d.bowler_id) SELECT COUNT(*) FROM bat JOIN bowl ON bowl.match_id = bat.match_id AND bowl.pid = bat.pid WHERE bat.r >= 30 AND bowl.w >= 2
model_sql:
WITH player_match_batting AS (
  SELECT 
    match_id,
    striker_id AS player_id,
    SUM(runs_of_bat) AS runs_off_bat
  FROM deliveries
  WHERE innings IN (1, 2)
  GROUP BY match_id, striker_id
),
player_match_bowling AS (
  SELECT 
    match_id,
    bowler_id AS player_id,
    COUNT(*) AS wickets
  FROM deliveries
  WHERE innings IN (1, 2) AND player_dismissed_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY match_id, bowler_id
)
SELECT COUNT(*) AS count
FROM player_match_batting pmb
INNER JOIN player_match_bowling pmbo 
  ON pmb.match_id = pmbo.match_id 
  AND pmb.player_id = pmbo.player_id
WHERE pmb.runs_off_bat >= 30 AND pmbo.wickets >= 2

question: Among batters with at least 250 runs off the bat (regular innings), who has the highest batting average (runs divided by number of times dismissed, excluding 'retired hurt')? Give the name and the average.
gold_sql: WITH r AS (SELECT striker_id AS pid, SUM(runs_of_bat) AS runs FROM deliveries WHERE innings <= 2 GROUP BY striker_id HAVING SUM(runs_of_bat) >= 250), o AS (SELECT player_dismissed_id AS pid, COUNT(*) AS outs FROM deliveries WHERE player_dismissed_id IS NOT NULL AND wicket_type != 'retired hurt' AND innings <= 2 GROUP BY player_dismissed_id) SELECT p.player_name, r.runs * 1.0 / o.outs AS bat_avg FROM r JOIN o ON o.pid = r.pid JOIN players p ON p.player_id = r.pid ORDER BY bat_avg DESC LIMIT 1
model_sql:
WITH batter_stats AS (
  SELECT
    d.striker_id,
    p.player_name,
    SUM(d.runs_of_bat) as total_runs,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN d.player_dismissed_id = d.striker_id AND d.wicket_type != 'retired hurt' THEN 1 END) as dismissals
  FROM deliveries d
  JOIN players p ON d.striker_id = p.player_id
  WHERE d.innings IN (1, 2)
  GROUP BY d.striker_id, p.player_name
  HAVING SUM(d.runs_of_bat) >= 250
)
SELECT
  player_name,
  CAST(total_runs AS REAL) / NULLIF(dismissals, 0) as average
FROM batter_stats
WHERE dismissals > 0
ORDER BY average DESC
LIMIT 1

question: For how many players in batting_stats does the runs column differ from the runs off the bat they scored in deliveries during the matches covered by match_results?
gold_sql: WITH s AS (SELECT striker_id AS pid, SUM(runs_of_bat) AS r FROM deliveries WHERE match_id IN (SELECT match_id FROM match_results) GROUP BY striker_id) SELECT COUNT(*) FROM batting_stats b LEFT JOIN s ON s.pid = b.player_id WHERE COALESCE(s.r, 0) != b.runs
model_sql:
WITH matches_with_results AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT m.match_id
  FROM matches m
  INNER JOIN match_results mr ON m.match_id = mr.match_id
),
actual_runs AS (
  SELECT 
    d.striker_id,
    SUM(d.runs_of_bat) as actual_runs_of_bat
  FROM deliveries d
  INNER JOIN matches_with_results mwr ON d.match_id = mwr.match_id
  GROUP BY d.striker_id
)
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT bs.player_id)
FROM batting_stats bs
LEFT JOIN actual_runs ar ON bs.player_id = ar.striker_id
WHERE ar.actual_runs_of_bat IS NOT NULL
  AND bs.runs != ar.actual_runs_of_bat

question: How many times did a player take at least one catch AND score at least 50 runs off the bat in the same match (regular innings)?
gold_sql: WITH bat AS (SELECT match_id, striker_id AS pid FROM deliveries WHERE innings <= 2 GROUP BY match_id, striker_id HAVING SUM(runs_of_bat) >= 50), ct AS (SELECT DISTINCT d.match_id, f.player_id AS pid FROM delivery_fielders f JOIN deliveries d ON d.delivery_id = f.delivery_id WHERE d.wicket_type = 'caught' AND d.innings <= 2) SELECT COUNT(*) FROM bat JOIN ct ON ct.match_id = bat.match_id AND ct.pid = bat.pid
model_sql:
WITH catches AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT
    d.match_id,
    df.player_id,
    d.innings
  FROM deliveries d
  JOIN delivery_fielders df ON d.delivery_id = df.delivery_id
  WHERE d.innings IN (1, 2)
    AND d.wicket_type = 'caught'
),
batting_50_plus AS (
  SELECT
    d.match_id,
    d.striker_id AS player_id,
    d.innings,
    SUM(d.runs_of_bat) AS runs_off_bat
  FROM deliveries d
  WHERE d.innings IN (1, 2)
  GROUP BY d.match_id, d.striker_id, d.innings
  HAVING SUM(d.runs_of_bat) >= 50
)
SELECT COUNT(*) AS count
FROM catches c
JOIN batting_50_plus b
  ON c.match_id = b.match_id
  AND c.player_id = b.player_id

question: Among completed matches in match_results played at a venue that is the home ground (venues.home_team) of one of the two teams, what percentage were won by that venue's home team?

question: For which bowling team (full name) did overseas bowlers take the highest share of its bowler-credited wickets? Give the team and the percentage.

question: For the season's top run scorer (runs off the bat), in which city or cities did they score the most runs? Return all tied cities with the runs.

question: Compare the average team innings total (runs off the bat plus extras, regular innings) when a team bats at one of its own home venues versus anywhere else. Ignore matches marked abandoned in match_results. Return labels 'home' and 'away' with the averages.
gold_sql: WITH t AS (SELECT d.match_id, d.batting_team, SUM(d.runs_of_bat + d.extras) AS r FROM deliveries d WHERE d.innings <= 2 AND d.match_id NOT IN (SELECT match_id FROM match_results WHERE match_result = 'abandoned') GROUP BY d.match_id, d.batting_team) SELECT CASE WHEN v.home_team = t.batting_team THEN 'home' ELSE 'away' END AS side, AVG(t.r) FROM t JOIN matches m ON m.match_id = t.match_id JOIN venues v ON v.venue_id = m.venue_id GROUP BY side

    AVG(total_runs) AS avg_total

question: Among bowlers with at least 120 legal deliveries (regular innings), who has the best economy rate (runs conceded per 6 legal balls; byes and leg-byes are not charged)? Give the name and economy.
gold_sql: SELECT p.player_name, 6.0 * SUM(d.runs_of_bat + CASE WHEN d.wide = 1 OR d.noballs = 1 THEN d.extras ELSE 0 END) / SUM(CASE WHEN d.wide = 0 AND d.noballs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS econ FROM deliveries d JOIN players p ON p.player_id = d.bowler_id WHERE d.innings <= 2 GROUP BY p.player_id HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN d.wide = 0 AND d.noballs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) >= 120 ORDER BY econ ASC LIMIT 1
model_sql:
SELECT p.player_name,
       SUM(CASE WHEN d.wide = 0 AND d.noballs = 0 THEN
                CASE WHEN d.byes = 1 OR d.legbyes = 1 THEN 0 ELSE d.runs_of_bat + d.extras END
           ELSE 0 END) * 6.0 /
       SUM(CASE WHEN d.wide = 0 AND d.noballs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS economy
FROM deliveries d
JOIN players p ON p.player_id = d.bowler_id
WHERE d.innings IN (1, 2)
GROUP BY d.bowler_id
HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN d.wide = 0 AND d.noballs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) >= 120
ORDER BY economy ASC
LIMIT 1

question: Which bowling team had the best (lowest) economy in the death overs (overs 15-19, regular innings)? Economy = runs conceded per 6 legal balls (byes and leg-byes not charged). Give the full team name and economy.
gold_sql: SELECT t.team_name, 6.0 * SUM(d.runs_of_bat + CASE WHEN d.wide = 1 OR d.noballs = 1 THEN d.extras ELSE 0 END) / SUM(CASE WHEN d.wide = 0 AND d.noballs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS econ FROM deliveries d JOIN teams t ON t.team_code = d.bowling_team WHERE d.innings <= 2 AND d.over_no >= 15 GROUP BY t.team_code ORDER BY econ ASC LIMIT 1

       SUM(d.runs_of_bat + d.extras - d.legbyes - d.byes) * 6.0 /

question: In how many matches does match_results.highscore differ from the runs off the bat that the listed top scorer actually made in that match according to deliveries (regular innings only)?
gold_sql: WITH s AS (SELECT match_id, striker_id, SUM(runs_of_bat) AS r FROM deliveries WHERE innings <= 2 GROUP BY match_id, striker_id) SELECT COUNT(*) FROM match_results mr JOIN s ON s.match_id = mr.match_id AND s.striker_id = mr.top_scorer_id WHERE mr.highscore != s.r

SELECT COUNT(*) AS mismatch_count
FROM (
    SELECT mr.match_id,
           mr.highscore,
           COALESCE(SUM(d.runs_of_bat), 0) AS actual_runs
    FROM match_results mr
    LEFT JOIN deliveries d
        ON d.match_id = mr.match_id
       AND d.innings IN (1, 2)
       AND d.striker_id = mr.top_scorer_id
    GROUP BY mr.match_id, mr.highscore
) t
WHERE t.actual_runs <> t.highscore

question: Which team(s) used the most different players this season (anyone who batted, bowled or fielded for it)? Return all tied teams (full names) with the number of players.

question: Which team had the biggest increase in its innings total (runs off the bat plus extras, regular innings) from one match to its next match in date order? Ignore matches marked abandoned in match_results. Give the full team name and the increase.
gold_sql: WITH t AS (SELECT d.match_id, d.batting_team, SUM(d.runs_of_bat + d.extras) AS r FROM deliveries d WHERE d.innings <= 2 AND d.match_id NOT IN (SELECT match_id FROM match_results WHERE match_result = 'abandoned') GROUP BY d.match_id, d.batting_team), g AS (SELECT t.batting_team, t.r - LAG(t.r) OVER (PARTITION BY t.batting_team ORDER BY m.date, m.match_id) AS diff FROM t JOIN matches m ON m.match_id = t.match_id) SELECT tm.team_name, g.diff FROM g JOIN teams tm ON tm.team_code = g.batting_team ORDER BY g.diff DESC LIMIT 1
model_sql:
WITH team_innings AS (
    SELECT d.match_id,
           d.batting_team AS team_code,
           m.date,
           SUM(d.runs_of_bat + d.extras) AS total_runs
    FROM deliveries d
    JOIN matches m ON d.match_id = m.match_id
    WHERE d.innings IN (1,2)
      AND NOT EXISTS (
            SELECT 1 FROM match_results mr
            WHERE mr.match_id = d.match_id AND mr.match_result = 'abandoned'
      )
    GROUP BY d.match_id, d.batting_team, m.date
),
ordered AS (
    SELECT *,
           LAG(total_runs) OVER (PARTITION BY team_code ORDER BY date, match_id) AS prev_runs
    FROM team_innings
)
SELECT t.team_name, (o.total_runs - o.prev_runs) AS increase
FROM ordered o
JOIN teams t ON o.team_code = t.team_code
WHERE o.prev_runs IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY increase DESC
LIMIT 1

question: What is the median first-innings score in match_results (ignore matches without a score)? With an even count, the median is the average of the two middle values.
gold_sql: WITH s AS (SELECT first_ings_score AS x, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY first_ings_score) AS rn, COUNT(*) OVER () AS n FROM match_results WHERE first_ings_score IS NOT NULL) SELECT AVG(x) FROM s WHERE rn IN ((n + 1) / 2, (n + 2) / 2)
model_sql:
WITH ordered AS (
    SELECT
        first_ings_score,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY first_ings_score) AS rn,
        COUNT(*) OVER () AS cnt
    FROM match_results
    WHERE first_ings_score IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT AVG(first_ings_score) AS median_first_innings_score
FROM ordered
WHERE rn IN ((cnt + 1) / 2, (cnt + 2) / 2)

question: How many ducks were there this season? A duck is a player dismissed in a match (regular innings, excluding 'retired hurt') who scored zero runs off the bat in that match, including players dismissed without facing a ball.
gold_sql: WITH dis AS (SELECT DISTINCT match_id, player_dismissed_id AS pid FROM deliveries WHERE player_dismissed_id IS NOT NULL AND wicket_type != 'retired hurt' AND innings <= 2), runs AS (SELECT match_id, striker_id AS pid, SUM(runs_of_bat) AS r FROM deliveries WHERE innings <= 2 GROUP BY match_id, striker_id) SELECT COUNT(*) FROM dis LEFT JOIN runs ON runs.match_id = dis.match_id AND runs.pid = dis.pid WHERE COALESCE(runs.r, 0) = 0
model_sql:
WITH dismissals AS (
    SELECT match_id, player_dismissed_id AS player_id
    FROM deliveries
    WHERE wicket_type IS NOT NULL
      AND wicket_type <> 'retired hurt'
      AND innings IN (1,2)
),
runs AS (
    SELECT match_id, striker_id AS player_id, SUM(runs_of_bat) AS total_runs
    FROM deliveries
    WHERE innings IN (1,2)

question: What is the highest score by a batter who was NOT dismissed in that match (a not-out innings, regular innings only)? Give the name and runs.
gold_sql: WITH s AS (SELECT match_id, striker_id, SUM(runs_of_bat) AS r FROM deliveries WHERE innings <= 2 GROUP BY match_id, striker_id) SELECT p.player_name, s.r FROM s JOIN players p ON p.player_id = s.striker_id WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM deliveries d WHERE d.match_id = s.match_id AND d.player_dismissed_id = s.striker_id AND d.innings <= 2) ORDER BY s.r DESC LIMIT 1
model_sql:
WITH inn AS (
    SELECT match_id, innings, striker_id, SUM(runs_of_bat) AS runs
    FROM deliveries
    WHERE innings IN (1,2)
    GROUP BY match_id, innings, striker_id
),
dis AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT match_id, innings, player_dismissed_id
    FROM deliveries
    WHERE player_dismissed_id IS NOT NULL AND innings IN (1,2)
)
SELECT p.player_name, i.runs
FROM inn i
JOIN players p ON p.player_id = i.striker_id
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM dis d
    WHERE d.match_id = i.match_id
      AND d.innings = i.innings
      AND d.player_dismissed_id = i.striker_id
)
ORDER BY i.runs DESC
LIMIT 1

question: Which bowler bowled the most maiden overs? A maiden is an over (same match, innings, over number and bowler; regular innings) with exactly 6 legal deliveries and zero runs conceded (byes and leg-byes are not charged). Give the name and count.
gold_sql: WITH o AS (SELECT d.bowler_id, SUM(d.runs_of_bat + CASE WHEN d.wide = 1 OR d.noballs = 1 THEN d.extras ELSE 0 END) AS conceded, SUM(CASE WHEN d.wide = 0 AND d.noballs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS legal FROM deliveries d WHERE d.innings <= 2 GROUP BY d.match_id, d.innings, d.over_no, d.bowler_id) SELECT p.player_name, COUNT(*) AS maidens FROM o JOIN players p ON p.player_id = o.bowler_id WHERE o.conceded = 0 AND o.legal = 6 GROUP BY p.player_id ORDER BY maidens DESC LIMIT 1
model_sql:
WITH over_stats AS (
  SELECT
    match_id,
    innings,
    over_no,
    bowler_id,
    SUM(CASE WHEN wide = 0 AND noballs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS legal_balls,
    SUM(CASE WHEN byes = 0 AND legbyes = 0 THEN runs_of_bat + extras ELSE runs_of_bat END) AS conceded_runs
  FROM deliveries
  WHERE innings IN (1, 2)
  GROUP BY match_id, innings, over_no, bowler_id
),
maidens AS (
  SELECT bowler_id, COUNT(*) AS maiden_overs
  FROM over_stats
  WHERE legal_balls = 6 AND conceded_runs = 0
  GROUP BY bowler_id
)
SELECT p.player_name, m.maiden_overs
FROM maidens m
JOIN players p ON p.player_id = m.bowler_id
ORDER BY m.maiden_overs DESC
LIMIT 1

question: How many times did a player score at least 30 runs off the bat AND take at least 2 bowler-credited wickets in the same match (regular innings)?
gold_sql: WITH bat AS (SELECT match_id, striker_id AS pid, SUM(runs_of_bat) AS r FROM deliveries WHERE innings <= 2 GROUP BY match_id, striker_id), bowl AS (SELECT d.match_id, d.bowler_id AS pid, COUNT(*) AS w FROM deliveries d WHERE d.innings <= 2 AND d.player_dismissed_id IS NOT NULL AND d.wicket_type NOT IN ('run out','retired hurt','obstructing the field') GROUP BY d.match_id, d.bowler_id) SELECT COUNT(*) FROM bat JOIN bowl ON bowl.match_id = bat.match_id AND bowl.pid = bat.pid WHERE bat.r >= 30 AND bowl.w >= 2

WITH batting AS (
    SELECT match_id, striker_id AS player_id, SUM(runs_of_bat) AS runs
    FROM deliveries

bowling AS (

      AND wicket_type IN ('bowled','caught','lbw','stumped','hit wicket')
    GROUP BY match_id, bowler_id
    HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2

question: Among batters with at least 250 runs off the bat (regular innings), who has the highest batting average (runs divided by number of times dismissed, excluding 'retired hurt')? Give the name and the average.
gold_sql: WITH r AS (SELECT striker_id AS pid, SUM(runs_of_bat) AS runs FROM deliveries WHERE innings <= 2 GROUP BY striker_id HAVING SUM(runs_of_bat) >= 250), o AS (SELECT player_dismissed_id AS pid, COUNT(*) AS outs FROM deliveries WHERE player_dismissed_id IS NOT NULL AND wicket_type != 'retired hurt' AND innings <= 2 GROUP BY player_dismissed_id) SELECT p.player_name, r.runs * 1.0 / o.outs AS bat_avg FROM r JOIN o ON o.pid = r.pid JOIN players p ON p.player_id = r.pid ORDER BY bat_avg DESC LIMIT 1
model_sql:
WITH runs AS (
  SELECT striker_id AS player_id, SUM(runs_of_bat) AS total_runs
  FROM deliveries
  WHERE innings IN (1,2)
  GROUP BY striker_id
),
outs AS (
  SELECT player_dismissed_id AS player_id, COUNT(*) AS dismissals
  FROM deliveries
  WHERE innings IN (1,2)
    AND player_dismissed_id IS NOT NULL
    AND wicket_type != 'retired hurt'
  GROUP BY player_dismissed_id
),
stats AS (
  SELECT r.player_id, r.total_runs,
         COALESCE(o.dismissals,0) AS dismissals,
         CAST(r.total_runs AS REAL) / COALESCE(o.dismissals,0) AS batting_average
  FROM runs r
  LEFT JOIN outs o ON r.player_id = o.player_id
  WHERE r.total_runs >= 250 AND COALESCE(o.dismissals,0) > 0
)
SELECT p.player_name, s.batting_average
FROM stats s
JOIN players p ON p.player_id = s.player_id
WHERE s.batting_average = (SELECT MAX(batting_average) FROM stats)
ORDER BY p.player_name

question: For how many players in batting_stats does the runs column differ from the runs off the bat they scored in deliveries during the matches covered by match_results?

question: How many times did a player take at least one catch AND score at least 50 runs off the bat in the same match (regular innings)?
gold_sql: WITH bat AS (SELECT match_id, striker_id AS pid FROM deliveries WHERE innings <= 2 GROUP BY match_id, striker_id HAVING SUM(runs_of_bat) >= 50), ct AS (SELECT DISTINCT d.match_id, f.player_id AS pid FROM delivery_fielders f JOIN deliveries d ON d.delivery_id = f.delivery_id WHERE d.wicket_type = 'caught' AND d.innings <= 2) SELECT COUNT(*) FROM bat JOIN ct ON ct.match_id = bat.match_id AND ct.pid = bat.pid

question: Among completed matches in match_results played at a venue that is the home ground (venues.home_team) of one of the two teams, what percentage were won by that venue's home team?

question: Which batter scored the most runs off the bat against a single bowler this season? Give the batter's name, the bowler's name and the runs.
gold_sql: SELECT s.player_name, b.player_name, SUM(d.runs_of_bat) AS r FROM deliveries d JOIN players s ON s.player_id = d.striker_id JOIN players b ON b.player_id = d.bowler_id GROUP BY d.striker_id, d.bowler_id ORDER BY r DESC LIMIT 1

SELECT p1.player_name AS batter, p2.player_name AS bowler, SUM(d.runs_of_bat) AS runs
FROM deliveries d
JOIN players p1 ON p1.player_id = d.striker_id
JOIN players p2 ON p2.player_id = d.bowler_id

question: For which bowling team (full name) did overseas bowlers take the highest share of its bowler-credited wickets? Give the team and the percentage.
gold_sql: WITH w AS (SELECT d.bowling_team, b.nationality FROM deliveries d JOIN players b ON b.player_id = d.bowler_id WHERE d.player_dismissed_id IS NOT NULL AND d.wicket_type NOT IN ('run out','retired hurt','obstructing the field')) SELECT t.team_name, 100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN w.nationality = 'Overseas' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*) AS pct FROM w JOIN teams t ON t.team_code = w.bowling_team GROUP BY t.team_code ORDER BY pct DESC LIMIT 1
model_sql:
WITH bowler_wkts AS (
    SELECT d.bowling_team,
           p.nationality,
           1 AS wkt
    FROM deliveries d
    JOIN players p ON p.player_id = d.bowler_id
    WHERE d.player_dismissed_id IS NOT NULL
      AND d.wicket_type NOT IN ('run out', 'obstructing the field', 'retired hurt')
),
agg AS (
    SELECT bowling_team,
           SUM(wkt) AS total_wkts,
           SUM(CASE WHEN nationality = 'Overseas' THEN wkt ELSE 0 END) AS overseas_wkts
    FROM bowler_wkts
    GROUP BY bowling_team
)
SELECT t.team_name,
       (a.overseas_wkts * 100.0 / a.total_wkts) AS overseas_pct
FROM agg a
JOIN teams t ON t.team_code = a.bowling_team

LIMIT 1

question: For the season's top run scorer (runs off the bat), in which city or cities did they score the most runs? Return all tied cities with the runs.
gold_sql: WITH c AS (SELECT v.city, SUM(d.runs_of_bat) AS r, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY SUM(d.runs_of_bat) DESC) AS rk FROM deliveries d JOIN matches m ON m.match_id = d.match_id JOIN venues v ON v.venue_id = m.venue_id WHERE d.striker_id = (SELECT striker_id FROM deliveries GROUP BY striker_id ORDER BY SUM(runs_of_bat) DESC LIMIT 1) GROUP BY v.city) SELECT city, r FROM c WHERE rk = 1
model_sql:
WITH top_scorer AS (
    SELECT striker_id
    FROM deliveries
    GROUP BY striker_id
    ORDER BY SUM(runs_of_bat) DESC
    LIMIT 1
),
city_runs AS (
    SELECT v.city, SUM(d.runs_of_bat) AS runs
    FROM deliveries d
    JOIN matches m ON d.match_id = m.match_id
    JOIN venues v ON m.venue_id = v.venue_id
    WHERE d.striker_id = (SELECT striker_id FROM top_scorer)
    GROUP BY v.city
),
max_runs AS (
    SELECT MAX(runs) AS max_runs FROM city_runs
)
SELECT cr.city, cr.runs
FROM city_runs cr, max_runs mr
WHERE cr.runs = mr.max_runs

question: Compare the average team innings total (runs off the bat plus extras, regular innings) when a team bats at one of its own home venues versus anywhere else. Ignore matches marked abandoned in match_results. Return labels 'home' and 'away' with the averages.
gold_sql: WITH t AS (SELECT d.match_id, d.batting_team, SUM(d.runs_of_bat + d.extras) AS r FROM deliveries d WHERE d.innings <= 2 AND d.match_id NOT IN (SELECT match_id FROM match_results WHERE match_result = 'abandoned') GROUP BY d.match_id, d.batting_team) SELECT CASE WHEN v.home_team = t.batting_team THEN 'home' ELSE 'away' END AS side, AVG(t.r) FROM t JOIN matches m ON m.match_id = t.match_id JOIN venues v ON v.venue_id = m.venue_id GROUP BY side
model_sql:
WITH innings_totals AS (
    SELECT
        d.match_id,
        d.innings,
        d.batting_team,
        SUM(d.runs_of_bat + d.extras) AS total_runs,
        v.home_team
    FROM deliveries d
    JOIN matches m ON d.match_id = m.match_id
    JOIN venues v ON m.venue_id = v.venue_id
    LEFT JOIN match_results mr ON d.match_id = mr.match_id
    WHERE d.innings IN (1, 2)
      AND (mr.match_result IS NULL OR mr.match_result != 'abandoned')
    GROUP BY d.match_id, d.innings, d.batting_team
)
SELECT
    CASE WHEN batting_team = home_team THEN 'home' ELSE 'away' END AS label,
    AVG(total_runs) AS average_innings_total
FROM innings_totals
GROUP BY label
ORDER BY label

question: How many centuries (100+ runs off the bat in a match) were scored in a losing cause? Only matches with a completed result in match_results can be judged.
gold_sql: WITH c AS (SELECT d.match_id, d.batting_team FROM deliveries d WHERE d.innings <= 2 GROUP BY d.match_id, d.striker_id HAVING SUM(d.runs_of_bat) >= 100) SELECT COUNT(*) FROM c JOIN match_results r ON r.match_id = c.match_id WHERE r.match_result = 'completed' AND r.match_winner != c.batting_team

question: Among bowlers with at least 120 legal deliveries (regular innings), who has the best economy rate (runs conceded per 6 legal balls; byes and leg-byes are not charged)? Give the name and economy.
gold_sql: SELECT p.player_name, 6.0 * SUM(d.runs_of_bat + CASE WHEN d.wide = 1 OR d.noballs = 1 THEN d.extras ELSE 0 END) / SUM(CASE WHEN d.wide = 0 AND d.noballs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS econ FROM deliveries d JOIN players p ON p.player_id = d.bowler_id WHERE d.innings <= 2 GROUP BY p.player_id HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN d.wide = 0 AND d.noballs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) >= 120 ORDER BY econ ASC LIMIT 1
model_sql:
WITH bowler_stats AS (
    SELECT
        d.bowler_id,
        SUM(d.runs_of_bat + (d.extras - d.byes - d.legbyes)) AS runs_conceded,
        COUNT(*) AS legal_balls
    FROM deliveries d
    WHERE d.innings IN (1, 2)
      AND d.wide = 0
      AND d.noballs = 0
    GROUP BY d.bowler_id
    HAVING legal_balls >= 120
)
SELECT p.player_name, (bs.runs_conceded * 6.0 / bs.legal_balls) AS economy
FROM bowler_stats bs
JOIN players p ON bs.bowler_id = p.player_id
ORDER BY economy ASC
LIMIT 1

question: Which bowling team had the best (lowest) economy in the death overs (overs 15-19, regular innings)? Economy = runs conceded per 6 legal balls (byes and leg-byes not charged). Give the full team name and economy.
gold_sql: SELECT t.team_name, 6.0 * SUM(d.runs_of_bat + CASE WHEN d.wide = 1 OR d.noballs = 1 THEN d.extras ELSE 0 END) / SUM(CASE WHEN d.wide = 0 AND d.noballs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS econ FROM deliveries d JOIN teams t ON t.team_code = d.bowling_team WHERE d.innings <= 2 AND d.over_no >= 15 GROUP BY t.team_code ORDER BY econ ASC LIMIT 1
model_sql:
WITH death_balls AS (
    SELECT d.bowling_team,
           d.runs_of_bat,
           d.extras,
           d.byes,
           d.legbyes,
           d.wide,
           d.noballs
    FROM deliveries d
    WHERE d.innings IN (1, 2)
      AND d.over_no BETWEEN 14 AND 18
),
team_stats AS (
    SELECT bowling_team,
           SUM(CASE WHEN byes = 0 AND legbyes = 0 THEN runs_of_bat + extras ELSE runs_of_bat END) AS runs_conceded,
           COUNT(CASE WHEN wide = 0 AND noballs = 0 THEN 1 END) AS legal_balls
    FROM death_balls
    GROUP BY bowling_team
)
SELECT t.team_name, (ts.runs_conceded * 1.0 / ts.legal_balls) * 6 AS economy
FROM team_stats ts
JOIN teams t ON ts.bowling_team = t.team_code
ORDER BY economy ASC
LIMIT 1

question: In how many matches does match_results.highscore differ from the runs off the bat that the listed top scorer actually made in that match according to deliveries (regular innings only)?
gold_sql: WITH s AS (SELECT match_id, striker_id, SUM(runs_of_bat) AS r FROM deliveries WHERE innings <= 2 GROUP BY match_id, striker_id) SELECT COUNT(*) FROM match_results mr JOIN s ON s.match_id = mr.match_id AND s.striker_id = mr.top_scorer_id WHERE mr.highscore != s.r

FROM match_results mr
LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT match_id, striker_id, SUM(runs_of_bat) AS actual_runs
    FROM deliveries
    WHERE innings IN (1, 2)
    GROUP BY match_id, striker_id

WHERE mr.top_scorer_id IS NOT NULL
  AND mr.highscore IS NOT NULL

question: Which team(s) used the most different players this season (anyone who batted, bowled or fielded for it)? Return all tied teams (full names) with the number of players.
gold_sql: WITH used AS (SELECT batting_team AS team, striker_id AS pid FROM deliveries UNION SELECT bowling_team, bowler_id FROM deliveries UNION SELECT d.bowling_team, f.player_id FROM delivery_fielders f JOIN deliveries d ON d.delivery_id = f.delivery_id), c AS (SELECT team, COUNT(*) AS n, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC) AS rk FROM used GROUP BY team) SELECT t.team_name, c.n FROM c JOIN teams t ON t.team_code = c.team WHERE c.rk = 1
model_sql:
WITH participant_roles AS (
    SELECT batting_team AS team_code, striker_id AS player_id FROM deliveries
    UNION
    SELECT bowling_team AS team_code, bowler_id AS player_id FROM deliveries
    UNION
    SELECT d.bowling_team AS team_code, df.player_id
    FROM delivery_fielders df
    JOIN deliveries d ON df.delivery_id = d.delivery_id
),

question: Which team had the biggest increase in its innings total (runs off the bat plus extras, regular innings) from one match to its next match in date order? Ignore matches marked abandoned in match_results. Give the full team name and the increase.
gold_sql: WITH t AS (SELECT d.match_id, d.batting_team, SUM(d.runs_of_bat + d.extras) AS r FROM deliveries d WHERE d.innings <= 2 AND d.match_id NOT IN (SELECT match_id FROM match_results WHERE match_result = 'abandoned') GROUP BY d.match_id, d.batting_team), g AS (SELECT t.batting_team, t.r - LAG(t.r) OVER (PARTITION BY t.batting_team ORDER BY m.date, m.match_id) AS diff FROM t JOIN matches m ON m.match_id = t.match_id) SELECT tm.team_name, g.diff FROM g JOIN teams tm ON tm.team_code = g.batting_team ORDER BY g.diff DESC LIMIT 1
model_sql:
WITH team_match_totals AS (
    SELECT 
        m.match_id,
        m.date,
        d.batting_team,
        SUM(d.runs_of_bat + d.extras) AS innings_total
    FROM deliveries d
    JOIN matches m ON d.match_id = m.match_id
    WHERE d.innings IN (1, 2)
      AND m.match_id NOT IN (
          SELECT match_id FROM match_results WHERE match_result = 'abandoned'
      )
    GROUP BY m.match_id, m.date, d.batting_team
),
team_match_ordered AS (
    SELECT 
        batting_team,
        date,
        innings_total,
        LAG(innings_total) OVER (PARTITION BY batting_team ORDER BY date, match_id) AS prev_innings_total
    FROM team_match_totals
)
SELECT 
    t.team_name,
    (innings_total - prev_innings_total) AS increase
FROM team_match_ordered tmo
JOIN teams t ON tmo.batting_team = t.team_code
WHERE prev_innings_total IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY increase DESC
LIMIT 1

question: What is the median first-innings score in match_results (ignore matches without a score)? With an even count, the median is the average of the two middle values.
gold_sql: WITH s AS (SELECT first_ings_score AS x, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY first_ings_score) AS rn, COUNT(*) OVER () AS n FROM match_results WHERE first_ings_score IS NOT NULL) SELECT AVG(x) FROM s WHERE rn IN ((n + 1) / 2, (n + 2) / 2)
model_sql:
WITH ordered AS (
  SELECT first_ings_score,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY first_ings_score) AS rn,
         COUNT(*) OVER () AS cnt
  FROM match_results
  WHERE first_ings_score IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT AVG(first_ings_score) AS median
FROM ordered
WHERE rn IN ((cnt + 1) / 2, (cnt + 2) / 2)

question: How many ducks were there this season? A duck is a player dismissed in a match (regular innings, excluding 'retired hurt') who scored zero runs off the bat in that match, including players dismissed without facing a ball.
gold_sql: WITH dis AS (SELECT DISTINCT match_id, player_dismissed_id AS pid FROM deliveries WHERE player_dismissed_id IS NOT NULL AND wicket_type != 'retired hurt' AND innings <= 2), runs AS (SELECT match_id, striker_id AS pid, SUM(runs_of_bat) AS r FROM deliveries WHERE innings <= 2 GROUP BY match_id, striker_id) SELECT COUNT(*) FROM dis LEFT JOIN runs ON runs.match_id = dis.match_id AND runs.pid = dis.pid WHERE COALESCE(runs.r, 0) = 0
model_sql:
WITH dismissals AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT match_id, player_dismissed_id
    FROM deliveries
    WHERE innings IN (1, 2)
      AND wicket_type IS NOT NULL
      AND wicket_type != 'retired hurt'
),
batting_runs AS (
    SELECT match_id, striker_id, SUM(runs_of_bat) AS total_runs
    FROM deliveries
    WHERE innings IN (1, 2)
    GROUP BY match_id, striker_id
)
SELECT COUNT(*) AS duck_count
FROM dismissals d
LEFT JOIN batting_runs b
  ON d.match_id = b.match_id
 AND d.player_dismissed_id = b.striker_id
WHERE COALESCE(b.total_runs, 0) = 0

question: What is the highest score by a batter who was NOT dismissed in that match (a not-out innings, regular innings only)? Give the name and runs.
gold_sql: WITH s AS (SELECT match_id, striker_id, SUM(runs_of_bat) AS r FROM deliveries WHERE innings <= 2 GROUP BY match_id, striker_id) SELECT p.player_name, s.r FROM s JOIN players p ON p.player_id = s.striker_id WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM deliveries d WHERE d.match_id = s.match_id AND d.player_dismissed_id = s.striker_id AND d.innings <= 2) ORDER BY s.r DESC LIMIT 1
model_sql:
SELECT p.player_name, SUM(d.runs_of_bat) AS runs
FROM deliveries d
JOIN players p ON p.player_id = d.striker_id
WHERE d.innings IN (1, 2)
  AND NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM deliveries d2
    WHERE d2.match_id = d.match_id
      AND d2.player_dismissed_id = d.striker_id
      AND d2.innings IN (1, 2)
  )
GROUP BY d.match_id, d.striker_id, p.player_name
ORDER BY runs DESC
LIMIT 1

question: Which bowler bowled the most maiden overs? A maiden is an over (same match, innings, over number and bowler; regular innings) with exactly 6 legal deliveries and zero runs conceded (byes and leg-byes are not charged). Give the name and count.
gold_sql: WITH o AS (SELECT d.bowler_id, SUM(d.runs_of_bat + CASE WHEN d.wide = 1 OR d.noballs = 1 THEN d.extras ELSE 0 END) AS conceded, SUM(CASE WHEN d.wide = 0 AND d.noballs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS legal FROM deliveries d WHERE d.innings <= 2 GROUP BY d.match_id, d.innings, d.over_no, d.bowler_id) SELECT p.player_name, COUNT(*) AS maidens FROM o JOIN players p ON p.player_id = o.bowler_id WHERE o.conceded = 0 AND o.legal = 6 GROUP BY p.player_id ORDER BY maidens DESC LIMIT 1
model_sql:
WITH over_stats AS (
    SELECT
        match_id,
        innings,
        over_no,
        bowler_id,
        COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE wide = 0 AND noballs = 0) AS legal_balls,
        SUM(CASE WHEN byes = 0 AND legbyes = 0 THEN runs_of_bat + extras ELSE 0 END) AS runs_conceded
    FROM deliveries
    WHERE innings IN (1, 2)
    GROUP BY match_id, innings, over_no, bowler_id
),
maiden_overs AS (
    SELECT bowler_id
    FROM over_stats
    WHERE legal_balls = 6 AND runs_conceded = 0
),
bowler_maiden_counts AS (
    SELECT
        bowler_id,
        COUNT(*) AS maiden_count
    FROM maiden_overs
    GROUP BY bowler_id
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT
        bowler_id,
        maiden_count,
        RANK() OVER (ORDER BY maiden_count DESC) AS rnk
    FROM bowler_maiden_counts
)
SELECT
    p.player_name,
    r.maiden_count
FROM ranked r
JOIN players p ON r.bowler_id = p.player_id
WHERE r.rnk = 1

question: How many times did a player score at least 30 runs off the bat AND take at least 2 bowler-credited wickets in the same match (regular innings)?
gold_sql: WITH bat AS (SELECT match_id, striker_id AS pid, SUM(runs_of_bat) AS r FROM deliveries WHERE innings <= 2 GROUP BY match_id, striker_id), bowl AS (SELECT d.match_id, d.bowler_id AS pid, COUNT(*) AS w FROM deliveries d WHERE d.innings <= 2 AND d.player_dismissed_id IS NOT NULL AND d.wicket_type NOT IN ('run out','retired hurt','obstructing the field') GROUP BY d.match_id, d.bowler_id) SELECT COUNT(*) FROM bat JOIN bowl ON bowl.match_id = bat.match_id AND bowl.pid = bat.pid WHERE bat.r >= 30 AND bowl.w >= 2
model_sql:
WITH batting AS (
    SELECT match_id, striker_id AS player_id, SUM(runs_of_bat) AS runs
    FROM deliveries
    WHERE innings IN (1, 2)
    GROUP BY match_id, striker_id
    HAVING SUM(runs_of_bat) >= 30
),
bowling AS (
    SELECT match_id, bowler_id AS player_id, COUNT(*) AS wickets
    FROM deliveries
    WHERE innings IN (1, 2)
      AND wicket_type IN ('bowled', 'caught', 'lbw', 'stumped', 'hit wicket')
    GROUP BY match_id, bowler_id
    HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2
)
SELECT COUNT(*) AS times
FROM batting b
JOIN bowling w ON b.match_id = w.match_id AND b.player_id = w.player_id

question: Among batters with at least 250 runs off the bat (regular innings), who has the highest batting average (runs divided by number of times dismissed, excluding 'retired hurt')? Give the name and the average.
gold_sql: WITH r AS (SELECT striker_id AS pid, SUM(runs_of_bat) AS runs FROM deliveries WHERE innings <= 2 GROUP BY striker_id HAVING SUM(runs_of_bat) >= 250), o AS (SELECT player_dismissed_id AS pid, COUNT(*) AS outs FROM deliveries WHERE player_dismissed_id IS NOT NULL AND wicket_type != 'retired hurt' AND innings <= 2 GROUP BY player_dismissed_id) SELECT p.player_name, r.runs * 1.0 / o.outs AS bat_avg FROM r JOIN o ON o.pid = r.pid JOIN players p ON p.player_id = r.pid ORDER BY bat_avg DESC LIMIT 1
model_sql:
WITH batter_runs AS (
    SELECT striker_id, SUM(runs_of_bat) AS total_runs
    FROM deliveries
    WHERE innings IN (1, 2)
    GROUP BY striker_id
    HAVING total_runs >= 250
),
dismissals AS (
    SELECT player_dismissed_id, COUNT(*) AS dismissals
    FROM deliveries
    WHERE innings IN (1, 2)
      AND wicket_type IS NOT NULL
      AND wicket_type != 'retired hurt'
    GROUP BY player_dismissed_id
)
SELECT p.player_name, br.total_runs * 1.0 / d.dismissals AS average
FROM batter_runs br
JOIN dismissals d ON br.striker_id = d.player_dismissed_id
JOIN players p ON br.striker_id = p.player_id
ORDER BY average DESC

question: For how many players in batting_stats does the runs column differ from the runs off the bat they scored in deliveries during the matches covered by match_results?

question: Which batter scored the most runs off the bat against a single bowler this season? Give the batter's name, the bowler's name and the runs.

question: For which bowling team (full name) did overseas bowlers take the highest share of its bowler-credited wickets? Give the team and the percentage.
gold_sql: WITH w AS (SELECT d.bowling_team, b.nationality FROM deliveries d JOIN players b ON b.player_id = d.bowler_id WHERE d.player_dismissed_id IS NOT NULL AND d.wicket_type NOT IN ('run out','retired hurt','obstructing the field')) SELECT t.team_name, 100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN w.nationality = 'Overseas' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*) AS pct FROM w JOIN teams t ON t.team_code = w.bowling_team GROUP BY t.team_code ORDER BY pct DESC LIMIT 1

           d.bowler_id,

    WHERE d.wicket_type IN ('bowled', 'caught', 'lbw', 'stumped', 'hit wicket', 'obstructing the field')

FROM team_shares

question: For the season's top run scorer (runs off the bat), in which city or cities did they score the most runs? Return all tied cities with the runs.

question: Among bowlers with at least 120 legal deliveries (regular innings), who has the best economy rate (runs conceded per 6 legal balls; byes and leg-byes are not charged)? Give the name and economy.
gold_sql: SELECT p.player_name, 6.0 * SUM(d.runs_of_bat + CASE WHEN d.wide = 1 OR d.noballs = 1 THEN d.extras ELSE 0 END) / SUM(CASE WHEN d.wide = 0 AND d.noballs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS econ FROM deliveries d JOIN players p ON p.player_id = d.bowler_id WHERE d.innings <= 2 GROUP BY p.player_id HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN d.wide = 0 AND d.noballs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) >= 120 ORDER BY econ ASC LIMIT 1
model_sql:
WITH bowler_stats AS (
  SELECT
    bowler_id,
    SUM(runs_of_bat + extras - byes - legbyes) AS runs_conceded,
    SUM(CASE WHEN wide = 0 AND noballs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS legal_balls
  FROM deliveries
  WHERE innings IN (1, 2)
  GROUP BY bowler_id
)

  p.player_name,
  bs.runs_conceded * 6.0 / bs.legal_balls AS economy
FROM bowler_stats bs
JOIN players p ON p.player_id = bs.bowler_id
WHERE bs.legal_balls >= 120
ORDER BY economy ASC
LIMIT 1

question: Which team had the biggest increase in its innings total (runs off the bat plus extras, regular innings) from one match to its next match in date order? Ignore matches marked abandoned in match_results. Give the full team name and the increase.
gold_sql: WITH t AS (SELECT d.match_id, d.batting_team, SUM(d.runs_of_bat + d.extras) AS r FROM deliveries d WHERE d.innings <= 2 AND d.match_id NOT IN (SELECT match_id FROM match_results WHERE match_result = 'abandoned') GROUP BY d.match_id, d.batting_team), g AS (SELECT t.batting_team, t.r - LAG(t.r) OVER (PARTITION BY t.batting_team ORDER BY m.date, m.match_id) AS diff FROM t JOIN matches m ON m.match_id = t.match_id) SELECT tm.team_name, g.diff FROM g JOIN teams tm ON tm.team_code = g.batting_team ORDER BY g.diff DESC LIMIT 1
model_sql:

  SELECT d.batting_team, d.match_id, m.date,
         SUM(d.runs_of_bat + d.extras) AS total
  FROM deliveries d
  JOIN matches m ON m.match_id = d.match_id
  WHERE d.innings IN (1, 2)
    AND d.match_id NOT IN (SELECT match_id FROM match_results WHERE match_result = 'abandoned')
  GROUP BY d.batting_team, d.match_id, m.date
),

question: What is the median first-innings score in match_results (ignore matches without a score)? With an even count, the median is the average of the two middle values.

question: Which bowler bowled the most maiden overs? A maiden is an over (same match, innings, over number and bowler; regular innings) with exactly 6 legal deliveries and zero runs conceded (byes and leg-byes are not charged). Give the name and count.
gold_sql: WITH o AS (SELECT d.bowler_id, SUM(d.runs_of_bat + CASE WHEN d.wide = 1 OR d.noballs = 1 THEN d.extras ELSE 0 END) AS conceded, SUM(CASE WHEN d.wide = 0 AND d.noballs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS legal FROM deliveries d WHERE d.innings <= 2 GROUP BY d.match_id, d.innings, d.over_no, d.bowler_id) SELECT p.player_name, COUNT(*) AS maidens FROM o JOIN players p ON p.player_id = o.bowler_id WHERE o.conceded = 0 AND o.legal = 6 GROUP BY p.player_id ORDER BY maidens DESC LIMIT 1

         SUM(CASE WHEN wide = 0 AND noballs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS legal_balls,

  FROM deliveries
  WHERE innings IN (1, 2)
  GROUP BY match_id, innings, over_no, bowler_id

FROM over_agg o
JOIN players p ON p.player_id = o.bowler_id

question: Among batters with at least 250 runs off the bat (regular innings), who has the highest batting average (runs divided by number of times dismissed, excluding 'retired hurt')? Give the name and the average.

question: Compare the average team innings total (runs off the bat plus extras, regular innings) when a team bats at one of its own home venues versus anywhere else. Ignore matches marked abandoned in match_results. Return labels 'home' and 'away' with the averages.

question: Which team(s) used the most different players this season (anyone who batted, bowled or fielded for it)? Return all tied teams (full names) with the number of players.
gold_sql: WITH used AS (SELECT batting_team AS team, striker_id AS pid FROM deliveries UNION SELECT bowling_team, bowler_id FROM deliveries UNION SELECT d.bowling_team, f.player_id FROM delivery_fielders f JOIN deliveries d ON d.delivery_id = f.delivery_id), c AS (SELECT team, COUNT(*) AS n, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC) AS rk FROM used GROUP BY team) SELECT t.team_name, c.n FROM c JOIN teams t ON t.team_code = c.team WHERE c.rk = 1

question: Which team had the biggest increase in its innings total (runs off the bat plus extras, regular innings) from one match to its next match in date order? Ignore matches marked abandoned in match_results. Give the full team name and the increase.
gold_sql: WITH t AS (SELECT d.match_id, d.batting_team, SUM(d.runs_of_bat + d.extras) AS r FROM deliveries d WHERE d.innings <= 2 AND d.match_id NOT IN (SELECT match_id FROM match_results WHERE match_result = 'abandoned') GROUP BY d.match_id, d.batting_team), g AS (SELECT t.batting_team, t.r - LAG(t.r) OVER (PARTITION BY t.batting_team ORDER BY m.date, m.match_id) AS diff FROM t JOIN matches m ON m.match_id = t.match_id) SELECT tm.team_name, g.diff FROM g JOIN teams tm ON tm.team_code = g.batting_team ORDER BY g.diff DESC LIMIT 1

        d.match_id,
        m.date,

    FROM deliveries d
    JOIN matches m ON d.match_id = m.match_id
    WHERE d.innings IN (1, 2)

question: What is the median first-innings score in match_results (ignore matches without a score)? With an even count, the median is the average of the two middle values.

    SELECT 
        first_ings_score,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY first_ings_score) AS rn,
        COUNT(*) OVER () AS total_count
    FROM match_results
    WHERE first_ings_score IS NOT NULL
)

FROM RankedScores
WHERE rn BETWEEN (total_count + 1) / 2 AND (total_count + 2) / 2

question: How many ducks were there this season? A duck is a player dismissed in a match (regular innings, excluding 'retired hurt') who scored zero runs off the bat in that match, including players dismissed without facing a ball.

question: Which bowler bowled the most maiden overs? A maiden is an over (same match, innings, over number and bowler; regular innings) with exactly 6 legal deliveries and zero runs conceded (byes and leg-byes are not charged). Give the name and count.

question: Compare the average team innings total (runs off the bat plus extras, regular innings) when a team bats at one of its own home venues versus anywhere else. Ignore matches marked abandoned in match_results. Return labels 'home' and 'away' with the averages.

question: Among bowlers with at least 120 legal deliveries (regular innings), who has the best economy rate (runs conceded per 6 legal balls; byes and leg-byes are not charged)? Give the name and economy.
gold_sql: SELECT p.player_name, 6.0 * SUM(d.runs_of_bat + CASE WHEN d.wide = 1 OR d.noballs = 1 THEN d.extras ELSE 0 END) / SUM(CASE WHEN d.wide = 0 AND d.noballs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS econ FROM deliveries d JOIN players p ON p.player_id = d.bowler_id WHERE d.innings <= 2 GROUP BY p.player_id HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN d.wide = 0 AND d.noballs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) >= 120 ORDER BY econ ASC LIMIT 1
model_sql:
WITH bowler_figures AS (
    SELECT
        d.bowler_id,
        SUM(CASE WHEN d.wide = 0 AND d.noballs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS legal_balls,
        SUM(
            d.runs_of_bat +
            CASE
                WHEN d.byes = 1 OR d.legbyes = 1 THEN 0
                ELSE d.extras
            END
        ) AS runs_conceded
    FROM deliveries AS d
    WHERE d.innings IN (1, 2)
    GROUP BY d.bowler_id
),
qualified AS (
    SELECT
        bowler_id,
        runs_conceded * 6.0 / legal_balls AS economy
    FROM bowler_figures
    WHERE legal_balls >= 120
)
SELECT
    p.player_name,
    q.economy
FROM qualified AS q
JOIN players AS p
    ON p.player_id = q.bowler_id
WHERE q.economy = (SELECT MIN(economy) FROM qualified)

question: Which team had the biggest increase in its innings total (runs off the bat plus extras, regular innings) from one match to its next match in date order? Ignore matches marked abandoned in match_results. Give the full team name and the increase.

question: What is the median first-innings score in match_results (ignore matches without a score)? With an even count, the median is the average of the two middle values.

question: Which bowler bowled the most maiden overs? A maiden is an over (same match, innings, over number and bowler; regular innings) with exactly 6 legal deliveries and zero runs conceded (byes and leg-byes are not charged). Give the name and count.

question: For how many players in batting_stats does the runs column differ from the runs off the bat they scored in deliveries during the matches covered by match_results?
gold_sql: WITH s AS (SELECT striker_id AS pid, SUM(runs_of_bat) AS r FROM deliveries WHERE match_id IN (SELECT match_id FROM match_results) GROUP BY striker_id) SELECT COUNT(*) FROM batting_stats b LEFT JOIN s ON s.pid = b.player_id WHERE COALESCE(s.r, 0) != b.runs
model_sql:
WITH delivery_runs AS (
    SELECT
        d.striker_id,
        SUM(d.runs_of_bat) AS runs
    FROM deliveries AS d
    JOIN match_results AS mr
        ON mr.match_id = d.match_id
    GROUP BY d.striker_id
)

FROM batting_stats AS bs

question: How many times did a player take at least one catch AND score at least 50 runs off the bat in the same match (regular innings)?
gold_sql: WITH bat AS (SELECT match_id, striker_id AS pid FROM deliveries WHERE innings <= 2 GROUP BY match_id, striker_id HAVING SUM(runs_of_bat) >= 50), ct AS (SELECT DISTINCT d.match_id, f.player_id AS pid FROM delivery_fielders f JOIN deliveries d ON d.delivery_id = f.delivery_id WHERE d.wicket_type = 'caught' AND d.innings <= 2) SELECT COUNT(*) FROM bat JOIN ct ON ct.match_id = bat.match_id AND ct.pid = bat.pid
model_sql:
WITH batting AS (
    SELECT
        match_id,
        striker_id AS player_id,
        SUM(runs_of_bat) AS runs
    FROM deliveries
    WHERE innings IN (1, 2)
    GROUP BY match_id, striker_id
    HAVING SUM(runs_of_bat) >= 50
),
catches AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        d.match_id,
        df.player_id
    FROM deliveries d
    JOIN delivery_fielders df
        ON df.delivery_id = d.delivery_id
    WHERE d.innings IN (1, 2)
      AND d.wicket_type = 'caught'
)

FROM batting b
JOIN catches c
    ON c.match_id = b.match_id

question: Which batter scored the most runs off the bat against a single bowler this season? Give the batter's name, the bowler's name and the runs.

    SUM(d.runs_of_bat) AS runs

question: For which bowling team (full name) did overseas bowlers take the highest share of its bowler-credited wickets? Give the team and the percentage.
gold_sql: WITH w AS (SELECT d.bowling_team, b.nationality FROM deliveries d JOIN players b ON b.player_id = d.bowler_id WHERE d.player_dismissed_id IS NOT NULL AND d.wicket_type NOT IN ('run out','retired hurt','obstructing the field')) SELECT t.team_name, 100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN w.nationality = 'Overseas' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*) AS pct FROM w JOIN teams t ON t.team_code = w.bowling_team GROUP BY t.team_code ORDER BY pct DESC LIMIT 1
model_sql:
WITH team_wickets AS (
    SELECT
        d.bowling_team,
        SUM(CASE WHEN p.nationality = 'Overseas' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS overseas_wickets,
        COUNT(*) AS total_wickets
    FROM deliveries AS d
    JOIN players AS p
        ON p.player_id = d.bowler_id
    WHERE d.wicket_type IN ('bowled', 'caught', 'hit wicket', 'lbw', 'stumped')
    GROUP BY d.bowling_team
)
SELECT
    t.team_name,
    tw.overseas_wickets * 100.0 / tw.total_wickets AS percentage
FROM team_wickets AS tw
JOIN teams AS t
    ON t.team_code = tw.bowling_team
ORDER BY percentage DESC
LIMIT 1

question: For the season's top run scorer (runs off the bat), in which city or cities did they score the most runs? Return all tied cities with the runs.
gold_sql: WITH c AS (SELECT v.city, SUM(d.runs_of_bat) AS r, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY SUM(d.runs_of_bat) DESC) AS rk FROM deliveries d JOIN matches m ON m.match_id = d.match_id JOIN venues v ON v.venue_id = m.venue_id WHERE d.striker_id = (SELECT striker_id FROM deliveries GROUP BY striker_id ORDER BY SUM(runs_of_bat) DESC LIMIT 1) GROUP BY v.city) SELECT city, r FROM c WHERE rk = 1
model_sql:
WITH player_runs AS (
    SELECT striker_id, SUM(runs_of_bat) AS total_runs
    FROM deliveries
    GROUP BY striker_id
),
top_scorers AS (
    SELECT striker_id
    FROM player_runs
    WHERE total_runs = (SELECT MAX(total_runs) FROM player_runs)
),
city_runs AS (
    SELECT d.striker_id, v.city, SUM(d.runs_of_bat) AS runs
    FROM deliveries AS d
    JOIN matches AS m ON m.match_id = d.match_id
    JOIN venues AS v ON v.venue_id = m.venue_id
    JOIN top_scorers AS ts ON ts.striker_id = d.striker_id
    GROUP BY d.striker_id, v.city
)
SELECT DISTINCT city, runs
FROM city_runs
WHERE runs = (
    SELECT MAX(cr.runs)
    FROM city_runs AS cr
    WHERE cr.striker_id = city_runs.striker_id
)

question: Compare the average team innings total (runs off the bat plus extras, regular innings) when a team bats at one of its own home venues versus anywhere else. Ignore matches marked abandoned in match_results. Return labels 'home' and 'away' with the averages.
gold_sql: WITH t AS (SELECT d.match_id, d.batting_team, SUM(d.runs_of_bat + d.extras) AS r FROM deliveries d WHERE d.innings <= 2 AND d.match_id NOT IN (SELECT match_id FROM match_results WHERE match_result = 'abandoned') GROUP BY d.match_id, d.batting_team) SELECT CASE WHEN v.home_team = t.batting_team THEN 'home' ELSE 'away' END AS side, AVG(t.r) FROM t JOIN matches m ON m.match_id = t.match_id JOIN venues v ON v.venue_id = m.venue_id GROUP BY side
model_sql:
WITH innings_totals AS (
    SELECT
        d.match_id,
        d.innings,
        d.batting_team,
        SUM(d.runs_of_bat + d.extras) AS total_runs,
        CASE WHEN v.home_team = d.batting_team THEN 'home' ELSE 'away' END AS location
    FROM deliveries AS d
    JOIN matches AS m ON m.match_id = d.match_id
    JOIN venues AS v ON v.venue_id = m.venue_id
    LEFT JOIN match_results AS mr ON mr.match_id = m.match_id
    WHERE d.innings IN (1, 2)
      AND (mr.match_result IS NULL OR mr.match_result <> 'abandoned')
    GROUP BY d.match_id, d.innings, d.batting_team, location
)
SELECT location, AVG(total_runs) AS average_total
FROM innings_totals
GROUP BY location

question: How many centuries (100+ runs off the bat in a match) were scored in a losing cause? Only matches with a completed result in match_results can be judged.
gold_sql: WITH c AS (SELECT d.match_id, d.batting_team FROM deliveries d WHERE d.innings <= 2 GROUP BY d.match_id, d.striker_id HAVING SUM(d.runs_of_bat) >= 100) SELECT COUNT(*) FROM c JOIN match_results r ON r.match_id = c.match_id WHERE r.match_result = 'completed' AND r.match_winner != c.batting_team

        d.batting_team,
        d.striker_id,

    FROM deliveries AS d

question: Among bowlers with at least 120 legal deliveries (regular innings), who has the best economy rate (runs conceded per 6 legal balls; byes and leg-byes are not charged)? Give the name and economy.
gold_sql: SELECT p.player_name, 6.0 * SUM(d.runs_of_bat + CASE WHEN d.wide = 1 OR d.noballs = 1 THEN d.extras ELSE 0 END) / SUM(CASE WHEN d.wide = 0 AND d.noballs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS econ FROM deliveries d JOIN players p ON p.player_id = d.bowler_id WHERE d.innings <= 2 GROUP BY p.player_id HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN d.wide = 0 AND d.noballs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) >= 120 ORDER BY econ ASC LIMIT 1
model_sql:
WITH bowler_economy AS (
    SELECT
        d.bowler_id,
        6.0 * SUM(
            d.runs_of_bat +
            CASE WHEN d.byes = 1 OR d.legbyes = 1 THEN 0 ELSE d.extras END
        ) / SUM(CASE WHEN d.wide = 0 AND d.noballs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS economy
    FROM deliveries AS d
    WHERE d.innings IN (1, 2)
    GROUP BY d.bowler_id
    HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN d.wide = 0 AND d.noballs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) >= 120
)
SELECT p.player_name, b.economy
FROM bowler_economy AS b
JOIN players AS p ON p.player_id = b.bowler_id
WHERE b.economy = (SELECT MIN(economy) FROM bowler_economy)

question: Which bowling team had the best (lowest) economy in the death overs (overs 15-19, regular innings)? Economy = runs conceded per 6 legal balls (byes and leg-byes not charged). Give the full team name and economy.
gold_sql: SELECT t.team_name, 6.0 * SUM(d.runs_of_bat + CASE WHEN d.wide = 1 OR d.noballs = 1 THEN d.extras ELSE 0 END) / SUM(CASE WHEN d.wide = 0 AND d.noballs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS econ FROM deliveries d JOIN teams t ON t.team_code = d.bowling_team WHERE d.innings <= 2 AND d.over_no >= 15 GROUP BY t.team_code ORDER BY econ ASC LIMIT 1
model_sql:
WITH team_economy AS (
    SELECT
        bowling_team,
        6.0 * SUM(runs_of_bat + extras - byes - legbyes)
            / SUM(CASE WHEN wide = 0 AND noballs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS economy
    FROM deliveries
    WHERE innings IN (1, 2)
      AND over_no BETWEEN 14 AND 19
    GROUP BY bowling_team
)
SELECT teams.team_name, team_economy.economy
FROM team_economy
JOIN teams ON teams.team_code = team_economy.bowling_team
ORDER BY team_economy.economy
LIMIT 1

question: In how many matches does match_results.highscore differ from the runs off the bat that the listed top scorer actually made in that match according to deliveries (regular innings only)?
gold_sql: WITH s AS (SELECT match_id, striker_id, SUM(runs_of_bat) AS r FROM deliveries WHERE innings <= 2 GROUP BY match_id, striker_id) SELECT COUNT(*) FROM match_results mr JOIN s ON s.match_id = mr.match_id AND s.striker_id = mr.top_scorer_id WHERE mr.highscore != s.r
model_sql:
WITH scorer_runs AS (
    SELECT
        mr.match_id,
        mr.highscore,
        COALESCE(SUM(d.runs_of_bat), 0) AS actual_runs
    FROM match_results AS mr
    LEFT JOIN deliveries AS d
        ON d.match_id = mr.match_id
       AND d.innings IN (1, 2)
       AND d.striker_id = mr.top_scorer_id
    GROUP BY mr.match_id, mr.highscore
)
SELECT COUNT(*)
FROM scorer_runs
WHERE highscore <> actual_runs

question: Which team(s) used the most different players this season (anyone who batted, bowled or fielded for it)? Return all tied teams (full names) with the number of players.
gold_sql: WITH used AS (SELECT batting_team AS team, striker_id AS pid FROM deliveries UNION SELECT bowling_team, bowler_id FROM deliveries UNION SELECT d.bowling_team, f.player_id FROM delivery_fielders f JOIN deliveries d ON d.delivery_id = f.delivery_id), c AS (SELECT team, COUNT(*) AS n, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC) AS rk FROM used GROUP BY team) SELECT t.team_name, c.n FROM c JOIN teams t ON t.team_code = c.team WHERE c.rk = 1
model_sql:
WITH participants AS (
    SELECT batting_team AS team_code, striker_id AS player_id
    FROM deliveries
    UNION
    SELECT bowling_team, bowler_id
    FROM deliveries
    UNION
    SELECT d.bowling_team, df.player_id
    FROM delivery_fielders AS df
    JOIN deliveries AS d ON d.delivery_id = df.delivery_id

team_counts AS (

JOIN teams AS t ON t.team_code = tc.team_code

question: Which team had the biggest increase in its innings total (runs off the bat plus extras, regular innings) from one match to its next match in date order? Ignore matches marked abandoned in match_results. Give the full team name and the increase.
gold_sql: WITH t AS (SELECT d.match_id, d.batting_team, SUM(d.runs_of_bat + d.extras) AS r FROM deliveries d WHERE d.innings <= 2 AND d.match_id NOT IN (SELECT match_id FROM match_results WHERE match_result = 'abandoned') GROUP BY d.match_id, d.batting_team), g AS (SELECT t.batting_team, t.r - LAG(t.r) OVER (PARTITION BY t.batting_team ORDER BY m.date, m.match_id) AS diff FROM t JOIN matches m ON m.match_id = t.match_id) SELECT tm.team_name, g.diff FROM g JOIN teams tm ON tm.team_code = g.batting_team ORDER BY g.diff DESC LIMIT 1
model_sql:
WITH team_match_totals AS (
    SELECT
        d.match_id,
        d.batting_team AS team_code,
        SUM(d.runs_of_bat + d.extras) AS innings_total,
        m.date
    FROM deliveries AS d
    JOIN matches AS m ON m.match_id = d.match_id
    LEFT JOIN match_results AS mr ON mr.match_id = m.match_id
    WHERE d.innings IN (1, 2)
      AND (mr.match_result IS NULL OR mr.match_result <> 'abandoned')
    GROUP BY d.match_id, d.batting_team, m.date
),
match_changes AS (
    SELECT
        team_code,
        innings_total - LAG(innings_total) OVER (
            PARTITION BY team_code
            ORDER BY date, match_id
        ) AS increase
    FROM team_match_totals
)
SELECT t.team_name, mc.increase
FROM match_changes AS mc
JOIN teams AS t ON t.team_code = mc.team_code
WHERE mc.increase IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY mc.increase DESC
LIMIT 1

question: What is the median first-innings score in match_results (ignore matches without a score)? With an even count, the median is the average of the two middle values.
gold_sql: WITH s AS (SELECT first_ings_score AS x, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY first_ings_score) AS rn, COUNT(*) OVER () AS n FROM match_results WHERE first_ings_score IS NOT NULL) SELECT AVG(x) FROM s WHERE rn IN ((n + 1) / 2, (n + 2) / 2)
model_sql:
WITH ranked AS (
    SELECT
        first_ings_score,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY first_ings_score) AS rn,
        COUNT(*) OVER () AS cnt
    FROM match_results
    WHERE first_ings_score IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT AVG(first_ings_score)
FROM ranked
WHERE rn IN ((cnt + 1) / 2, (cnt + 2) / 2)

question: How many ducks were there this season? A duck is a player dismissed in a match (regular innings, excluding 'retired hurt') who scored zero runs off the bat in that match, including players dismissed without facing a ball.
gold_sql: WITH dis AS (SELECT DISTINCT match_id, player_dismissed_id AS pid FROM deliveries WHERE player_dismissed_id IS NOT NULL AND wicket_type != 'retired hurt' AND innings <= 2), runs AS (SELECT match_id, striker_id AS pid, SUM(runs_of_bat) AS r FROM deliveries WHERE innings <= 2 GROUP BY match_id, striker_id) SELECT COUNT(*) FROM dis LEFT JOIN runs ON runs.match_id = dis.match_id AND runs.pid = dis.pid WHERE COALESCE(runs.r, 0) = 0
model_sql:
WITH dismissed AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT match_id, player_dismissed_id
    FROM deliveries
    WHERE innings IN (1, 2)
      AND player_dismissed_id IS NOT NULL
      AND wicket_type <> 'retired hurt'
),
player_runs AS (
    SELECT match_id, striker_id, SUM(runs_of_bat) AS runs
    FROM deliveries
    WHERE innings IN (1, 2)
    GROUP BY match_id, striker_id
)
SELECT COUNT(*)
FROM dismissed d
LEFT JOIN player_runs r
  ON r.match_id = d.match_id
 AND r.striker_id = d.player_dismissed_id
WHERE COALESCE(r.runs, 0) = 0

question: What is the highest score by a batter who was NOT dismissed in that match (a not-out innings, regular innings only)? Give the name and runs.
gold_sql: WITH s AS (SELECT match_id, striker_id, SUM(runs_of_bat) AS r FROM deliveries WHERE innings <= 2 GROUP BY match_id, striker_id) SELECT p.player_name, s.r FROM s JOIN players p ON p.player_id = s.striker_id WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM deliveries d WHERE d.match_id = s.match_id AND d.player_dismissed_id = s.striker_id AND d.innings <= 2) ORDER BY s.r DESC LIMIT 1
model_sql:
WITH innings_scores AS (
    SELECT
        d.match_id,
        d.innings,
        d.striker_id AS player_id,
        SUM(d.runs_of_bat) AS runs
    FROM deliveries AS d
    WHERE d.innings IN (1, 2)
    GROUP BY d.match_id, d.innings, d.striker_id
    HAVING NOT EXISTS (
        SELECT 1
        FROM deliveries AS dismissal
        WHERE dismissal.match_id = d.match_id
          AND dismissal.innings = d.innings
          AND dismissal.player_dismissed_id = d.striker_id
    )
)
SELECT p.player_name, s.runs
FROM innings_scores AS s
JOIN players AS p ON p.player_id = s.player_id
WHERE s.runs = (SELECT MAX(runs) FROM innings_scores)

question: Which bowler bowled the most maiden overs? A maiden is an over (same match, innings, over number and bowler; regular innings) with exactly 6 legal deliveries and zero runs conceded (byes and leg-byes are not charged). Give the name and count.
gold_sql: WITH o AS (SELECT d.bowler_id, SUM(d.runs_of_bat + CASE WHEN d.wide = 1 OR d.noballs = 1 THEN d.extras ELSE 0 END) AS conceded, SUM(CASE WHEN d.wide = 0 AND d.noballs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS legal FROM deliveries d WHERE d.innings <= 2 GROUP BY d.match_id, d.innings, d.over_no, d.bowler_id) SELECT p.player_name, COUNT(*) AS maidens FROM o JOIN players p ON p.player_id = o.bowler_id WHERE o.conceded = 0 AND o.legal = 6 GROUP BY p.player_id ORDER BY maidens DESC LIMIT 1
model_sql:
WITH over_totals AS (
    SELECT
        match_id,
        innings,
        over_no,
        bowler_id,
        COUNT(CASE WHEN wide = 0 AND noballs = 0 THEN 1 END) AS legal_deliveries,
        SUM(runs_of_bat + CASE WHEN byes = 1 OR legbyes = 1 THEN 0 ELSE extras END) AS runs_conceded
    FROM deliveries
    WHERE innings IN (1, 2)
    GROUP BY match_id, innings, over_no, bowler_id
),
maiden_counts AS (
    SELECT bowler_id, COUNT(*) AS maiden_overs
    FROM over_totals
    WHERE legal_deliveries = 6 AND runs_conceded = 0
    GROUP BY bowler_id
)
SELECT p.player_name, mc.maiden_overs
FROM maiden_counts AS mc
JOIN players AS p ON p.player_id = mc.bowler_id
WHERE mc.maiden_overs = (SELECT MAX(maiden_overs) FROM maiden_counts)

question: How many times did a player score at least 30 runs off the bat AND take at least 2 bowler-credited wickets in the same match (regular innings)?
gold_sql: WITH bat AS (SELECT match_id, striker_id AS pid, SUM(runs_of_bat) AS r FROM deliveries WHERE innings <= 2 GROUP BY match_id, striker_id), bowl AS (SELECT d.match_id, d.bowler_id AS pid, COUNT(*) AS w FROM deliveries d WHERE d.innings <= 2 AND d.player_dismissed_id IS NOT NULL AND d.wicket_type NOT IN ('run out','retired hurt','obstructing the field') GROUP BY d.match_id, d.bowler_id) SELECT COUNT(*) FROM bat JOIN bowl ON bowl.match_id = bat.match_id AND bowl.pid = bat.pid WHERE bat.r >= 30 AND bowl.w >= 2
model_sql:
WITH batting AS (
    SELECT match_id, striker_id AS player_id, SUM(runs_of_bat) AS runs
    FROM deliveries
    WHERE innings IN (1, 2)
    GROUP BY match_id, striker_id
),
bowling AS (
    SELECT match_id, bowler_id AS player_id, COUNT(*) AS wickets
    FROM deliveries
    WHERE innings IN (1, 2)
      AND player_dismissed_id IS NOT NULL
      AND wicket_type IN ('bowled', 'caught', 'hit wicket', 'lbw', 'stumped')
    GROUP BY match_id, bowler_id
)
SELECT COUNT(*)
FROM batting
JOIN bowling USING (match_id, player_id)
WHERE batting.runs >= 30

question: Among batters with at least 250 runs off the bat (regular innings), who has the highest batting average (runs divided by number of times dismissed, excluding 'retired hurt')? Give the name and the average.

question: Among bowlers with at least 120 legal deliveries (regular innings), who has the best economy rate (runs conceded per 6 legal balls; byes and leg-byes are not charged)? Give the name and economy.

    SELECT d.bowler_id AS player_id,

    FROM deliveries d
    WHERE d.innings IN (1,2)
      AND d.wide = 0
      AND d.noballs = 0
    GROUP BY d.bowler_id
    HAVING COUNT(*) >= 120
),

    FROM bowler_stats bs
),

)

JOIN min_econ m ON e.economy = m.min_economy
ORDER BY p.player_name

gold_sql: WITH o AS (SELECT d.bowler_id, SUM(d.runs_of_bat + CASE WHEN d.wide = 1 OR d.noballs = 1 THEN d.extras ELSE 0 END) AS conceded, SUM(CASE WHEN d.wide = 0 AND d.noballs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS legal FROM deliveries d WHERE d.innings <= 2 GROUP BY d.match_id, d.innings, d.over_no, d.bowler_id) SELECT p.player_name, COUNT(*) AS maidens FROM o JOIN players p ON p.player_id = o.bowler_id WHERE o.conceded = 0 AND o.legal = 6 GROUP BY p.player_id ORDER BY maidens DESC LIMIT 1

    SELECT
        bowler_id,
        match_id,
        innings,
        over_no,
        SUM(CASE WHEN wide = 0 AND noballs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS legal_deliveries,
        SUM(runs_of_bat + extras - byes - legbyes) AS runs_conceded
    FROM deliveries
    WHERE innings IN (1, 2)
    GROUP BY bowler_id, match_id, innings, over_no
    HAVING
        SUM(CASE WHEN wide = 0 AND noballs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 6
        AND SUM(runs_of_bat + extras - byes - legbyes) = 0
),
bowler_maiden_counts AS (
    SELECT
        bowler_id,
        COUNT(*) AS maiden_overs
    FROM over_stats

question: How many times did a player score at least 30 runs off the bat AND take at least 2 bowler-credited wickets in the same match (regular innings)?

FROM (

        p.player_id,
        SUM(CASE WHEN d.striker_id = p.player_id THEN d.runs_of_bat ELSE 0 END) AS runs,
        SUM(CASE
                WHEN d.bowler_id = p.player_id
                     AND d.wicket_type IS NOT NULL
